# Part 1: <section> {#sec-part1}

## A content slide {#sec-content-slide .smaller}

::: notes
`{.smaller}` is step 1 of the ladder and the default for a content slide.
:::

Prose is one sentence per line.
A revealed beat is three to six short lines, and `. . .` separates the beats.

. . .

The second beat lands here.

. . .

::: {.callout-note}
**A note carries background or further detail.**
The four callout types and their jobs are fixed in STYLE.md §3.
:::

## A dense block {#sec-dense-block .smaller}

Step 2 of the ladder: wrap the one dense block in `.small`, not the whole slide.

::: {.small}
| Step | What you produce |
|--:|---|
| 1 | The estimand, stated as a target quantity. |
| 2 | The data described: measurement, coverage, obvious issues. |
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
**Never write an inline `style="font-size: ..."`.**
The ladder is `{.smaller}`, then `.small`, then `.xsmall`, then split the slide.
:::

## Two columns {#sec-columns .smaller}

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
The wider column carries the argument.
Permitted widths are 50/50, 55/45, 45/55, 60/40, 40/60 and 33/33/33.
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
The narrower column carries the figure or the aside.
:::

::::

## An equation and a figure {#sec-crossrefs .smaller}

Every equation gets a label, and @eq-bayes-core is how you refer back to it.

$$
p(\theta \mid Y) \propto L(Y \mid \theta) \times p(\theta)
$$ {#eq-bayes-core}

```{r}
#| label: fig-template-example
#| fig-cap: "Replace this with a real figure. A caption is self-sufficient when a reader
#|   who sees only the plot and this sentence knows what is shown and why it matters."
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| dpi: 500
#| echo: false

library(tidyverse) # wrangling and visualization
library(ggpubr) # theme_pubr()

col_1 <- "steelblue"

set.seed(2026)
tibble(x = rnorm(200)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, fill = col_1, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  theme_pubr() +
  labs(x = "Value", y = "Count", title = "Placeholder figure")
```
